messages.content: I’m starting the next one: Denver to Minneapolis for an Eden Prairie training week. Core sessions are Tuesday through Thursday, but I need to travel Monday because there’s equipment setup and a training-case handoff. Can you sketch the first plan before I bother the client with a million questions?

Yes. I’d like to anchor it around the Monday handoff first, because that drives the flight choice. What do you know so far: Tuesday start time, rough Thursday wrap, exact training site, and whether the Monday handoff is early afternoon, late afternoon, or still unknown?

Tuesday starts at 8. Thursday should wrap by 3 if nobody hijacks the agenda. Site is in Eden Prairie, client dinner may be Bloomington-ish. Monday handoff is still fuzzy, just “Monday afternoon.” I’ll have one checked hard-sided training case plus my bag.

Given the checked case and a suburban drive after landing, I’d build around arriving with cushion, not just the nicest departure time. First-pass flight ranking: 1) late-morning nonstop DEN-MSP, landing early afternoon, best for bag claim, rental pickup, and getting to Eden Prairie without sweating the handoff. 2) afternoon nonstop, comfortable start but only safe if the handoff is late enough or can slide. 3) one-stop with a short connection only if nonstop fares are unreasonable; I would not add multiple stops for this trip.
The afternoon nonstop is tempting because I don’t love leaving Denver before lunch. If the handoff lands around four, is that still too cute?

Probably too tight. If an afternoon flight lands around 4 or later, you still have bag claim, rental-car pickup, and a 25-to-40-minute drive depending on traffic. That puts you at the client closer to 5:15 or 5:30. If they confirm a 4 p.m. handoff, I’d use the late-morning nonstop. If they say 5:30 or later, the afternoon nonstop becomes reasonable.
Okay. For hotels, I don’t need fancy, but keep it well reviewed, four-ish or better if possible. Pool and fitness are useful. Hot tub is nice, not a hill to die on.

Then I’d compare two areas. Eden Prairie hotel near the site: likely the practical winner for training mornings, setup runs, and avoiding cross-town traffic. I’d accept it if it has a solid guest rating, pool, and fitness, even if the hot tub is missing. Bloomington or airport-area suite hotel: stronger recovery amenities are more likely, and it may be convenient for dinner or the return flight, but it adds drive time before both training days.
Would you take the Bloomington suite just for the hot tub?

Not as the first choice for this schedule. Three training mornings plus Monday setup make the closer Eden Prairie hotel more valuable. I’d only pick Bloomington if the Eden Prairie rate is high, parking is annoying, or the closer property looks dated despite the rating.
Rental car seems unavoidable, right? Lab, hotel, dinner, and St. Paul maybe later are all spread out.

Yes, I’d plan on a rental car. Reserve a midsize SUV or standard crossover rather than the smallest sedan, mostly for the hard case and to keep materials out of sight. Pick up at MSP, return at MSP, pay-later if the rate is close, and keep fuel/parking receipts separate from meals.
What exactly do I need from the client before I book?

Ask for: the Monday handoff time, whether there is a loading dock or preferred entrance, where the case can be stored overnight, the final street address for Tuesday training, whether the Monday walkthrough is mandatory, dinner location and time, parking instructions, and whether rental car plus checked training case are reimbursable. Once the handoff time is confirmed, choose the outbound: late-morning if they need you before about 5, afternoon only if they explicitly make the handoff late.

messages.content: Client confirmed the Monday handoff: 2:30 p.m., then a short facility walkthrough. So the afternoon departure is dead, right?

Yes, I would not use the afternoon departure for that. With a checked training case, rental pickup, and the drive to Eden Prairie, it leaves no real recovery if anything slips. Look for the nonstop that lands around 1 or earlier; landing after 1:30 starts getting uncomfortable.
I’m seeing two nonstops that fit the day: 10:05 out of Denver landing MSP at 1:02, or 1:35 out landing 4:25. Later one is about $70 cheaper.

Take the 10:05. The $70 savings does not buy enough risk protection. Rough timeline: land 1:02, bag by about 1:25 if things behave, rental car by 1:45, Eden Prairie around 2:15 to 2:25. That is still a working timeline, not a leisurely one. The 4:25 arrival misses the handoff.

Hotel final choices: Eden Prairie property is 4.4, pool and fitness, no hot tub listed, eight minutes from the site. Bloomington suite is 4.5, pool, hot tub, fitness, breakfast, but 22 to 30 minutes from the site depending on traffic.

Book the Eden Prairie property Monday through Thursday. The shorter commute and easier Monday logistics outweigh the missing hot tub for this one. Add a quick call after booking to confirm pool and fitness hours and ask whether they have a whirlpool that just is not showing online, but treat the hot tub as a nice-to-have, not the deciding factor.
That’s where I was leaning. Dinner may be in Bloomington one night, but the training mornings matter more.
Agreed. A single Bloomington dinner is an easy drive. Building three mornings around that dinner would be backwards.
What car class should I book? They will reimburse rental and the one checked training case.

Book a midsize SUV or standard crossover, pay-later if possible. It gives you easier loading for the hard case and enough space to keep training materials low and covered. Use the company discount code, decline prepaid fuel unless it is required by policy, and return it at MSP before your flight.
Seat map is open on the 10:05. I’ll take a window if I can get one.

Choose an A or F seat, ideally forward of the wing but not in the last row. Since it is nonstop, you do not need to optimize for a connection, so take the best window that does not put you right by the lavatory.
Give me the booking order so I don’t cross-wire the expenses.

Book in this order: 1) 10:05 nonstop DEN-MSP for Monday, landing 1:02, and select the window seat immediately. 2) Add the checked training case to the flight record or note the reimbursable bag fee. 3) Book the Eden Prairie hotel Monday-Thursday on the cancellable corporate rate, then call to confirm pool, fitness hours, parking, and any hot tub status. 4) Reserve the midsize SUV or crossover from MSP with return timed for your Thursday evening flight. 5) Put the 2:30 handoff, facility walkthrough, and drive buffer on your calendar. 6) Save flight, hotel, car, and baggage receipts under the Eden Prairie training folder.

messages.content: New wrinkle on the Eden Prairie trip. The regional manager added a Thursday late-afternoon case review at a St. Paul partner clinic and asked if I can stay for a Friday morning supervisor debrief. I already have a Thursday evening return. Bad idea to keep it?

Keeping the Thursday return is likely a bad fit. You would either leave the St. Paul meeting early or rush from St. Paul to MSP in traffic, return the car, and check the training case. If the Friday debrief is real and reimbursed, I’d move the return to Friday.
Thursday review is 4:30 to maybe 5:45 near the St. Paul clinic. Friday debrief is same general area at 9:30. Do I keep the Eden Prairie hotel or move for the last night?

Two workable paths: keep Eden Prairie and absorb the backtracking, which is simplest for one hotel folio and case security; or check out Thursday morning and stay near St. Paul or the east side of MSP, which makes Friday easier and the airport return cleaner. Moving hotels is better only if the case can be secured during the Thursday meeting.
I don’t love the hard case sitting in the car all afternoon.
Then ask the Eden Prairie site or the St. Paul clinic whether they can lock the case in an office. If nobody can secure it, extend the Eden Prairie hotel one night and accept the extra drive.
If the manager confirms reimbursement, what exactly changes?

Change the return to Friday, add one rental-car day, add one hotel night, and note any extra parking. If you move hotels, keep clean folios: Monday-Thursday Eden Prairie, Thursday-Friday St. Paul or MSP-area. If you stay put, it is just an added Eden Prairie night plus the rental extension.
Should the Friday flight be afternoon or evening?

Aim for early-to-mid afternoon Friday from MSP. A 9:30 debrief should leave enough time for wrap-up, drive, fuel, rental return, bag check, and security without wasting the whole day. Do not change the ticket until the manager confirms the Friday debrief, reimbursement for the added hotel and car day, and whether secure case storage is available Thursday.
